To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

selective backpropagation can learn deep generative models for latent neural dynamics from data where the set of observed neurons changes at each time-step, and that these models can be used to infer neural population activity from sparsely-samples data.

(i) we introduce a novel neural network training algorithm, selective backpropagtion through time (SBT), which enables learning of deep latent dynamics models from data in which only a subset of variables are observed at each time step, and (ii) SBT enables more efficient and higher fidelity characterization of neural population activity, providing an avenue for significant power savings for neuroelectronic interfaces, and enabling accurate recovery of high frequency temporal structure in neural population activity from sparse, high bandwidth sampling
we introduce a novel training strategy, SBTT, for deep generative models that enables learning from spatio-temporal data with changing observation variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel machine learning techniques to extract the maximum information from neural data.
the fundamental question of how to infer latent dynamics of neural circuits from sparse, high-dimensional time series.
developing novel neural networks for efficient inference of neural population dynamics from sparsely-sampling electrophysiological recordings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach enables more efficient and higher fidelity characterization of neural population activity in electrophysiology and calcium imaging.
SBTT enables spatio-temporal inference of neuronal activity from sparse, low-bandwidth data, and can be combined with pretraining to further enhance performance.
our approach enables the use of deep learning for the analysis of neural population dynamics with spatio- temporal super-resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SBTT can be used to learn latent dynamics from data that are sparsely sampled in time, and that this can be used for spatio-temporal data compression and super-resolution.
we developed a novel neural network training method, selective backprop through time, that allows for learning deep generative models for spatio-temporal data.
we have demonstrated that deep learning models can be trained to infer missing samples in time series data, even when the set of observed samples changes at each time point.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible, and indeed beneficial, to use neural interfaces with lower bandwidths than currently possible, while retaining high fidelity of neural dynamics characterization.
it is possible for deep neural network models to learn from data in which only subsets of variables are observed at each time step, and that such models are capable of inferring missing variables.
it is possible, in principle, to learn deep generative models from data where the set of observed neurons changes at each time point.
